quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #15
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: How do you enter a freeway?

options.text: Signal, yield to other traffic, and match their speed.
Signal and enter. Other traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly to check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to other traffic, and match their speed.
questions.explanation: Signal before merging. Match the speed of traffic already on the freeway. Always yield to other vehicles when entering.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Watch for trucks.
Do not pass trucks.
Truck parking area ahead.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: When two cars reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car coming from the right.
The car coming from the left.
The driver who honks first.
The car traveling fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car coming from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without traffic control signs, yield to the vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Just before you change lanes.
At any time.
After you change lanes.
Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early so other drivers have time to see your plan and react safely.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: One-way traffic.
Intersection ahead.
Traffic entering from the right.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic entering from the right.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is entering your road from the right.

questions.question: A car is coming toward you on the left, and a bicyclist is on your right. What should you do?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Go between both of them.
Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
Pass the bike quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bike.
questions.explanation: Deal with one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then safely pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: How can you avoid making emergency stops while driving in traffic?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn others.
Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
Drive in the right lane only.
Drive slower than other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep a safe distance from other cars.
questions.explanation: A safe following distance gives you time to stop smoothly without sudden braking, which could cause the car behind you to crash.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill behind a heavy truck. What should you know?

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to pass the truck safely.
You may not be able to pass the truck legally.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit on hills. You cannot legally pass on hills with poor visibility. It may not be safe to pass either.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street and an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches. You must:

options.text: Turn on your flashers.
Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.
Slow down until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the nearest side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through an intersection with a yellow light?

options.text: When an emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
When pedestrians are crossing.
When you are turning right.
When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you can carefully continue through.

questions.question: New vehicles have warning lights on the dashboard. Which statement is correct?

options.text: All lights should turn on when you first turn the ignition key, before starting the engine.
No lights should turn on until the engine is running.
The lights should never turn on unless something is broken.
The lights will only turn on if the headlights are on.

questions.correctAnswerText: All lights should turn on when you first turn the ignition key, before starting the engine.
questions.explanation: All warning lights on the dashboard should turn on when you turn the ignition key. If a light does not turn on, the light itself is broken.

questions.question: You must stop for a school bus:

options.text: That is parked on the side of the road with no one in it.
When it comes toward you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are both on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when you see a school bus with flashing red lights. On a two-lane road, traffic going both ways must stop and stay stopped while the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is out.

questions.question: Bicyclists must not:

options.text: Carry passengers unless the bike is made for passengers.
Ride on the sidewalk anywhere.
Ride at night.
Ride on the road in a business district.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carry passengers unless the bike is made for passengers.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists cannot ride on sidewalks in business districts. In other areas, they can ride on sidewalks if they go 10 mph or slower and let pedestrians go first. Bicyclists can ride at night if they have a headlight and reflector. They should never carry passengers unless the bike is designed for it.

questions.question: When you cannot see well while driving, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Turn on your windshield wipers.
Look for the edge of the road to guide you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slowing down is the first thing you should do when you cannot see well or the road is dangerous.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign:

options.text: Warns about hazards or dangers ahead.
Tells you about school zones.
Tells you about parks and recreation areas.
Tells you where to find food and gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns about hazards or dangers ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about hazards or dangers ahead. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, it:

options.text: Slows your reaction time.
Makes you feel less confident.
Gets broken down faster by your body.
Helps you make better driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slows your reaction time.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, it slows your reaction time, makes you feel too confident, and causes you to make more mistakes.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate highway:

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder if you get tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes.
Change lanes as often as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes on an interstate. Only stop on the shoulder for emergencies. Change lanes only when needed. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a bike lane.
Within 12 inches of the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a bike lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane. When parking on the street, you must park within 12 inches of the edge of the road.

questions.question: If traffic lights at an intersection are not working because of a power outage:

options.text: Park your car off the road and wait for power to come back.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you are doing.
Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop sign.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection like a four-way stop. Yield to other drivers the same way you would at a four-way stop, then go through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection. The light is green but many cars are coming toward you. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection instead.
Wait at the crosswalk until traffic clears.
Wait in the middle of the intersection until traffic clears.
Go ahead because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the middle of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: When turning left with oncoming traffic, wait for the traffic to pass before turning. You can enter the intersection if the light is green and no other car is making a left turn ahead of you.

questions.question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?

options.text: Never put an infant or small child in the front seat of a car with airbags.
Airbags can hurt an infant or small child, even in a slow crash.
Make sure all passengers use a seat belt or child restraint.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always fasten your seat belt before driving. Make sure all passengers use seat belts or child restraints. Seat belts reduce your chance of being hurt or killed in a crash. Children 12 and under should sit in the back seat with proper restraints. Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front of a car with a front airbag.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Flagger ahead.
Lane ends.
Turn right or go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and dangers. This sign warns you that an intersection is ahead.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs mean:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell drivers to let trains pass at railroad crossings. Do not try to drive faster than a train to cross the tracks.

questions.question: Which light means you should slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means slow down and be careful. Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all cars are the same.
Do not tell your friend you are unfamiliar with the car.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn how the car works and where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn how the car works and where all the controls are.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, spend a few minutes learning where the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear shift, and horn are located. Check that the car is in good condition. Fix any problems before you drive.

questions.question: A single broken yellow line in the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken or dashed line means you can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the more force your car has if it hits something.

questions.question: When passing other vehicles, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn at least three times.
Move back into your lane within 10 feet of the other car.
You do not need to use your turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Move back into your lane only when you can see the front of the other car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They alert drivers to upcoming hazards. This sign warns that a traffic signal is ahead. Be ready to stop for a red or yellow light.

questions.question: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lay down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car. You will be found more easily if you stay with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car. You will be found more easily if you stay with your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you get stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are more likely to be found if you do not leave your vehicle. Walking around in a snowstorm can be unsafe.
